cases.explanation: 12 circles, then “+2 more joined · 26 open”: the joined testers beyond the circles, and the spots still open.

cases.title: §6 The Length cap
cases.explanation: With Ben ticked the hint next to Length reads “10–40 min (the $1,000 for calls with Ben Okafor)”: what's left of his $1,000 at the call's $150/h.

cases.title: §6 Too long
cases.explanation: 60 minutes turns the box red, with the line under the row: “At most 40 minutes: the $1,000 for calls with Ben Okafor on this test.” (the server refuses it too).

cases.title: §6 Booking within the $1,000
cases.explanation: Ticking Ben shows his cap in the Length hint; 60 minutes is red, with the line under the row.

cases.title: §7 No product tick
cases.explanation: The excerpt picker has no “Don't name the product” tick any more: an excerpt always reads “From Night Market demo”.

cases.title: §7 Asking for an excerpt
cases.explanation: Ben picks a paid answer, trims it and asks Nora: no product tick.

cases.title: §7 Pending when the NDA came
cases.explanation: Nora added an NDA after Ben asked: the request can still be allowed, and says it will stay hidden while the NDA is on.

cases.title: §7 Allowed into hidden
cases.explanation: Ben's list reads “Allowed · hidden while Night Market demo has an NDA”: it shows on his profile if the NDA is removed.

cases.title: §8 Old answers stay payable
cases.explanation: The Switch / Keep box for changed questions adds: “Switching means answering the new questions: send your updated answers. Answers you already sent stay payable at $10.00.” (the price they were sent at)

cases.title: §9 Not cut
cases.explanation: Nora ended Dee's work early during the call: Dee's call page keeps the room and keeps measuring.

cases.title: §9 On the test page
cases.explanation: Dee's row: “In progress: it ends when you both leave”.

cases.title: §9 On Dee's page
cases.explanation: Her work ended, and the call still reads “In progress”.

cases.title: §9 A call in progress is never cut
cases.explanation: Nora (left) and Dee (right) stay on the call page while Nora's End early goes through: neither page closes.

cases.title: §9 Then it ends
cases.explanation: Once both have left (the 5-minute gap), the call page reads “Call ended at <time>.” and its measured minutes are payable as usual.

cases.title: §10 and §12 The developer's call page
cases.explanation: Join opens the Jitsi room in a new tab, “Keep this page open: it measures the call.”, and the host tip “Join a few minutes early: Jitsi asks the host to sign in with Google, GitHub or Facebook.”

cases.title: §10 and §12 The tester's call page
cases.explanation: The same Join line, and “If Jitsi says it's waiting for the host, Nora Lane is on the way: keep this page open.”

cases.title: §12 The developer's reminder
cases.explanation: 15 minutes before: “Your call with Cam Lee on “Harbor Run: live” starts at <time>.” with “Open it a few minutes early: Jitsi asks the first person to sign in with Google, GitHub or Facebook.”

cases.title: §12 The tester's reminder
cases.explanation: “Your call with Nora Lane on “Harbor Run: live” starts at <time>.”

cases.title: §13 Before the call
cases.explanation: Join opens only 10 minutes before (“You can join from <time>.”); “Check your call setup” is there from booking on, with its line about signing in to Jitsi ahead of time.

cases.title: §13 On the call's row
cases.explanation: Each booked call in Cam's Live session has “Check your call setup” (a private practice room, never measured).

cases.title: §13 On the tester dashboard
cases.explanation: Upcoming calls shows the link once per call.

cases.title: §13 On the developer dashboard
cases.explanation: Nora's Calls box has it too.

sections.title: Batch 19 (Oct 28)
sections.explanation: Batch 19, item by item (§ numbers are the items in docs/BATCH-19.md): the “Closing soon” bell heading, rating on the paused banner, Pay again after a cancelled bank check, the Length row, the Let it go stop box, the Terms' How payments work, and the Charge tick and Open until line on Post and Edit.

cases.title: §1 Closing soon (developer)
cases.explanation: Nora's bell stacks the close-out reminders under one heading, “Closing soon: 2 tests”, instead of an entry with no title.

cases.title: §1 Opened (developer)
cases.explanation: Inside: “Pay Dee Park's work on “Kelp Forest: iPhone beta” by <date>” and the same for Sky Lab.

cases.title: §1 Closing soon (tester)
cases.explanation: Dee's bell stacks the close-out reminders under one heading, “Closing soon: 2 tests”, instead of an entry with no title.

cases.title: §1 Opened (tester)
cases.explanation: Inside: “Charge or let go of your work on “Kelp Forest: iPhone beta” by <date>” and the same for Sky Lab.

cases.title: §2 The paused banner lists rating
cases.explanation: The team paused the test while Nora's Rate box for Ana is open, so the last line reads “For now you can stop this test, or rate testers.”, built from what's really there.

cases.title: §5 The Length row keeps its shape
cases.explanation: With the red line showing, “Length”, the box and “min” stay on one line (no letter-by-letter wrapping on a phone) and the red line sits under the whole row.

cases.title: §5 The stop box names the press
cases.explanation: Ben's Let it go stops once for Nora's Stop: “Your Let it go didn't go through.” (it used to say Charge), then the stop and “Press Let it go again to go ahead.”

cases.title: §5 Let it go stops once
cases.explanation: Nora stops the test while Ben's page is open: his Let it go stops with “Your Let it go didn't go through.”, and the second press goes through.

cases.title: §5 The check cancelled
cases.explanation: Nora cancelled her bank's check: “Your bank didn't confirm the payment, so nothing was charged.” Pay is still there.

cases.title: §5 Pay again
cases.explanation: Pressing Pay again on the same answers is a new attempt with its own bank check (before this fix it failed with “Something went wrong on our side”).

cases.title: §5 Paid once
cases.explanation: Confirmed this time: Ana's written answers read “paid $10.00 of $10.00” (Pay more takes Pay's place); she is paid once and the cancelled attempt charged nothing.

cases.title: §5 Pay after a cancelled bank check
cases.explanation: Nora presses Pay, cancels her bank's check (nothing charged), presses Pay again on the same answers, confirms, and Ana is paid.

cases.title: §6 How payments work
cases.explanation: The Terms of Use open at section 4, How payments work (its own link): “Payment is for the work the tester sent…”, then short headed paragraphs, each with a one-line example, starting with Prices and the split.

cases.title: §6 One scroll further
cases.explanation: The next headed paragraphs of the same section, each in plain words with its example (the whole section runs from Prices and the split to Taxes and refunds).

cases.title: §7 The Charge tick
cases.explanation: Just above Post the test: “I understand that a tester can charge my card, up to the listing price, for work I haven't paid once 7 days have passed since they sent it and their own deadline has passed.” with the link “How payments work”.

cases.title: §7 Unticked, Post is refused
cases.explanation: The server refuses it with the red line at the tick, “Tick to confirm you understand how payments work.”, and the list above the button counts it.

cases.title: §7 and §8 Posting with the tick
cases.explanation: The Open until line follows the date; Post unticked is refused in red at the tick; ticked, the next press posts the test.

cases.title: §7 Edit, nothing changed
cases.explanation: Save is faded and there's no tick above it.

cases.title: §7 Edit, with a change
cases.explanation: Save is on, and the same tick appears just above it, required for this Save.

cases.title: §7 and §8 The tick on Edit
cases.explanation: No tick while nothing changed; moving Open until 5 days later updates the line and brings the tick above Save; ticked, Save goes through.

cases.title: §8 The Open until line on Post
cases.explanation: Under the date, live: “Testers can join until this date. Each gets 14 days from when they join, so someone joining on <Open until> has until <14 days later> to send work. You pay each piece within 7 days of it arriving, or the tester can charge you.”

cases.title: §8 It follows the date
cases.explanation: Open until 20 days ahead: “Each gets 20 days from when they join …” and the last day to send work moves with it.

cases.title: §8 The Open until line on Edit
cases.explanation: Moved 5 days later, the line counts the days after the change: “Each gets 19 days from when they join, so someone joining on <Open until> has until <19 days later> to send work. …”

sections.title: Batch 20 (Oct 29)
sections.explanation: Batch 20, item by item (§ numbers are the items in docs/BATCH-20.md): question lists in scroll boxes, the 20-question notice, Invite anyway naming every missing need, Invite stops only for required items, 18+ at sign-up, profile Open tests, no false overlap flash, the Alerts chip and menu in sync, 1-letter searches, Invite while full, call history boxes, Pay more stopping presses once, the pill while typing, Rate and call changes, Dispute at the max, admin-only accounts, blocked profiles, no reload under typing, number boxes, the Open until line, the updated-Terms tick, prices for ticked parts, “Worked with you on N tests”, ratings live, Switch never stopping the developer, Send after a change, 5-character reasons and Send with the required answer.

cases.title: §1 Two questions: no box
cases.explanation: On the join page, “Nora Lane wants to know” lists 2 questions as a plain list.

cases.title: §1 Twenty questions: a scroll box
cases.explanation: The same card with 20 questions: every question is inside a box about 3 questions tall that scrolls (no “+17 more”).

cases.title: §1 A long question inside the box
cases.explanation: Scrolled to question 4, a long one: it keeps its own 3-line clamp with “Show more” inside the box.

cases.title: §1 The answer form in a box
cases.explanation: With 6 questions, the questions and their answer boxes (each with its toolbar) sit in a box about 3 questions tall; “Anything else”, the “0 / 50,000” counter and Send my answers stay below it.

cases.title: §1 A red mistake scrolls the box
cases.explanation: Send with question 6 (required) empty: the box scrolls itself to question 6 and the red line sits right under its answer box: “Answer every required question before sending.”

cases.title: §1 Sending with a required answer missing
cases.explanation: The tester answers question 1 and presses Send my answers; the box scrolls down to question 6, the empty required one, with “Answer every required question before sending.” under it.

cases.title: §2 At 20, the notice
cases.explanation: The 20th question brings a blue line under the last one: “At most 20 questions.” (a notice, not a red mistake: Post still works).

cases.title: §2 Deleting one removes it
cases.explanation: Back to 19 questions, the line is gone.

cases.title: §2 The 20-question notice
cases.explanation: With 19 questions there's no line; typing the 20th shows “At most 20 questions.” under the list; deleting it takes the line away.

cases.title: §3 One line per tester, both kinds
cases.explanation: “Fen Bao doesn't list a language this test needs (Chinese or Portuguese).”; Gus Hale: only the device part; Hana Ito, missing both: one line naming the languages and the devices, the long device list cut to its first 3 with “+5 more”.

cases.title: §3 “+5 more” opens the rest in place
cases.explanation: Pressed, Hana Ito's line lists every device the test needs (Windows PC, Switch, VR headset, Steam Deck, iPhone, Android phone, iPad or Android tablet), with “fewer” to fold it back.

cases.title: §3 Five testers: a scroll box
cases.explanation: With 5 testers ticked, the 5 lines sit in a small box that scrolls (about 4 lines show at once); Invite anyway and Cancel stay below it.

cases.title: §3 Invite anyway names every missing need
cases.explanation: Three testers ticked: one line each naming the missing languages, devices or both, a long list opened with “+5 more”; then five testers: the lines scroll in a box above Invite anyway.

cases.title: §4 An unrelated change never stops Invite
cases.explanation: Kai Noor added French and PlayStation to their profile after the page loaded; this test only needs Chinese, so Invite went straight through: Invited lists “Kai Noor · waiting for them to join”.

cases.title: §4 A required item added: one line
cases.explanation: Lea Ford changed their profile twice; only the net change to what this test needs is listed, once: “Lea Ford now lists Chinese, which this test needs.” with one time (French and Xbox aren't mentioned).

cases.title: §4 Added then removed: no stop
cases.explanation: Mo Reid added Chinese and took it out again: the edits cancel out, so there's no “now lists” line; the press opens the usual box for what they're missing: “Mo Reid doesn't list a language this test needs (Chinese).”

cases.title: §4 Invite stops only for required items
cases.explanation: An unrelated profile change goes straight through; a tester adding the required Chinese stops Invite once with one line; added-then-removed gives no stop.

cases.title: §5 The age tick at sign-up
cases.explanation: Next to the Terms agreement, a second required tick: “I'm 18 or older.”

cases.title: §5 Unticked, Sign up is refused
cases.explanation: Red at the tick: “You must be 18 or older to use Playtest.”, listed under Sign up with “Fix the mistake above, then press Sign up again.”; no account is made (the red line sits between the box and its words, pushing “I'm 18 or older.” to the side).

cases.title: §5 The Google sign-up step
cases.explanation: After Google answers for a new account, one short step before the account exists: the Terms agreement and “I'm 18 or older.”, then Continue (staged here without Google).

cases.title: §5 Continue with neither tick
cases.explanation: Nothing is created: “Agree to the Terms of Use to sign up” is red at the Terms tick and listed under Continue (“Fix the mistake above, then press Continue again.”); the age tick isn't marked yet.

cases.title: §5 Terms ticked, age not
cases.explanation: The next Continue is refused at the age tick: “You must be 18 or older to use Playtest.”; still no account.

cases.title: §6 A full test you're working in
cases.explanation: “Harbor Run: invite only” is full (1 of 1, invite only), yet it stays on Nora Lane's profile for the tester working in it, with “You're in this test” (it opens their session page).

cases.title: §6 An open invite to a full test
cases.explanation: For an invited tester the same full test stays listed with “Full right now: your invite stays open” (it opens the join page).

cases.title: §6 A pending application
cases.explanation: “Sky Lab: apply to join” is listed with “Applied (waiting)” for the tester who applied; the full invite-only test isn't shown to them.

cases.title: §7 A weekly call, nothing else booked
cases.explanation: The tester (no calls or requests yet) fills in a time, Weekly, 4 calls, 30 minutes: no red line.

cases.title: §7 After the press: no red flash
cases.explanation: The request went through and the form cleared; at no moment after the press (checked every 0.1 s, then after the next poll) did a red “overlaps” line show. The request waits in Call requests: “weekly calls: Sun 3:00 PM · 4 calls from Sun, Nov 1, 3:00 PM · 30 min · Contract $30/h · asked by you”.

cases.title: §7 Request a time, no false overlap
cases.explanation: A tester with no other calls asks for a weekly call: no red “overlaps” line appears at any moment; the request goes straight into Call requests.

cases.title: §8 The chip in the stop box
cases.explanation: Next round stops once for the tester's new call request; under it: “Don't stop me for: Call changes”.

cases.title: §8 Pressed: “Call changes (off)”
cases.explanation: The chip saves the same setting the Alerts menu uses.

cases.title: §8 The Alerts menu agrees at once
cases.explanation: Opened right after, the menu shows “Call changes” ticked (and the button reads “Alerts (1 off)”).

cases.title: §8 Another tab too
cases.explanation: A second tab of the test page opened afterwards: its Alerts menu also has “Call changes” ticked.

cases.title: §8 Un-ticked in the menu, the chip comes back
cases.explanation: After un-ticking “Call changes” in Alerts, the stop box's chip reads “Call changes” again (pressable).

cases.title: §8 The chip and the menu in sync
cases.explanation: Next round stops for a call request; “Don't stop me for: Call changes” turns to “(off)”; the Alerts menu opened right after has it ticked; un-ticking it there turns the chip back.

cases.title: §9 One letter finds a one-letter name
cases.explanation: “z” finds the tester named “Z” (the exact match first) and “Zan Okoro” (a word starting with z), and other testers named Z… (greyed when they can't join this test), but not “Ozanne Wilde”.

cases.title: §9 From 3 letters, any part
cases.explanation: “zan” also finds “Ozanne Wilde” (the letters inside a word) next to “Zan Okoro”.

cases.title: §9 Searching from 1 character
cases.explanation: Typing “z” finds “Z” and “Zan Okoro”; typing on to “zan” adds “Ozanne Wilde”.

cases.title: §10 Full: Invite is disabled
cases.explanation: Every spot is taken (1 of 1): Invite is greyed with the line under it, “This test is full. Add spots in Edit to invite more people.” (“in Edit” opens Edit's spots); the tick on Bo Tran stays.

cases.title: §10 A spot opens: Invite is back, live
cases.explanation: The tester in the only spot left the test; without a reload the line goes, Invite lights up with Bo Tran still ticked, and the tester who left can be ticked again under “People you've worked with”.

cases.title: §10 Invite while full
cases.explanation: On a full test Invite is greyed with “This test is full. Add spots in Edit to invite more people.”; the tester in the only spot leaves and Invite comes back on its own.

cases.title: §11 The tester's Call history: 6 calls
cases.explanation: More than 3 past calls sit in a plain scroll box about 3 calls tall, newest first, every call inside (no “Show 3 more”).

cases.title: §11 The developer's “Calls (6)”
cases.explanation: In the tester's row, the 6 calls sit in a scroll box (about 5 show at once), newest first, each with its own controls inside (here “Pay it in Needs you ↑”).

cases.title: §11 A link to the 5th call
cases.explanation: Opened from a link to the 5th call (newest first), the Call history box opens already scrolled down so that call is in view.

cases.title: §11 A link to an older call
cases.explanation: The session page opens from a link to the 5th call: the Call history box opens scrolled down to that call.

cases.title: §12 A Pay more stops the tester's press once
cases.explanation: Pay more was missing from the tester's stop list: now the Cancel call press stops once with “Nora Lane paid you $2.50 more for your written answers” (Alerts On).

cases.title: §12 Pay more, then Cancel call
cases.explanation: The developer pays $2.50 more while the tester's page is open; the tester's Cancel call stops once naming it, and the second press cancels the call.

cases.title: §12 The developer's other tab
cases.explanation: A Pay more made in another tab stops Pay here once: “You paid Ana Silva $1.00 more for their written answers in another tab”.

cases.title: §12 Pay more from another tab
cases.explanation: The developer pays Ana $1.00 more in another tab; Pay on Cam's answers here stops once and lists it.

cases.title: §13 While typing: the pill, no scroll
cases.explanation: The developer requested a call while the tester was typing an answer: the page stays put and a small “1 new update ↑” pill shows at the bottom.

cases.title: §13 The line in the live box
cases.explanation: Pressing the pill goes up to the live box, which lists the request (“Nora Lane requested a call …”).

cases.title: §13 A call request while typing
cases.explanation: The tester keeps typing as the developer requests a call: no jump, the “1 new update ↑” pill appears; pressed, it goes up to the live box's line.

cases.title: §15 Paid below the listing
cases.explanation: Ana's written answers were paid $8.00 of the $10.00 listing, so “Dispute the pay” is open to them.

cases.title: §15 Nothing left to award
cases.explanation: After Nora's Pay more of $2.00 (“Extra $2.00”), the page's own refresh greys “Dispute the pay” with the line “Already paid the most a dispute could award, so there's nothing to dispute.”

cases.title: §15 Dispute greys out live
cases.explanation: Ana's page is open with “Dispute the pay”; Nora pays $2.00 more, reaching the $10.00 listing, and without a reload the button greys with “Already paid the most a dispute could award, so there's nothing to dispute.”

cases.title: §16 An admin's setup
cases.explanation: “Welcome to Playtest” asks only Name and Pronoun: no “I'm here to” (an admin account has no developer or tester side).

cases.title: §16 Then the console
cases.explanation: Continue goes to the admin console (/admin), which is an admin's home from then on.

cases.title: §16 Admin only
cases.explanation: The setup asks only Name and Pronoun; Continue opens the console; Post a test and the dashboard move the admin back to /admin (Find stays: the admin version).

cases.title: §17 Before the block
cases.explanation: Nora's profile as Ana sees it: the stats, Open tests listing “Sky Lab: tutorial” and “Harbor Run: first 3 levels”, then “Report Nora Lane” and “Block Nora Lane”.

cases.title: §17 You blocked them
cases.explanation: The profile still opens (name, stats, ratings); Open tests reads “You blocked Nora Lane, so their tests are hidden.”, and where Block was there's “Unblock Nora Lane” (Report Nora Lane stays).

cases.title: §17 They blocked you
cases.explanation: Nora opens Ana's profile: the normal header, “← Back” and “This profile isn't available.” (the block is never named).

cases.title: §17 An unknown profile
cases.explanation: A profile address that doesn't exist: the header, “← Back” and “This page doesn't exist.” instead of the bare 404 page.

cases.title: §17 Unblock
cases.explanation: One press, no confirm, and the profile comes back in full at once: Open tests lists both tests again, with “Block Nora Lane” back under Report.

cases.title: §17 Block and Unblock on a profile
cases.explanation: Ana blocks Nora from Nora's profile: it stays open with Unblock and the tests hidden; Unblock brings everything back at once.

cases.title: §18 Typing kept
cases.explanation: Ben joined while Nora was typing in Request a time: the page showed it without reloading (a marker set before the change was still there), and the ticked tester, the time and Length “45” stayed.

cases.title: §18 Never reload under typing
cases.explanation: Nora fills in Request a time; Ben joins meanwhile; the page brings him in without a reload and the typed time and Length stay.

cases.title: §19 Spots takes digits only
cases.explanation: Typing “-20” leaves “20” (the minus is ignored); typed one after the other: -20 → “20”, 0 → “”, 1e3 → “13”, 2.5 → “25”.

cases.title: §19 The arrow keys stop at the minimum
cases.explanation: From 1, the down arrow keeps “1”: it never goes to 0 or below.

cases.title: §19 Money boxes take no minus
cases.explanation: Typing “-12.50” into the written answers' price leaves “12.50”.

cases.title: §19 Number boxes
cases.explanation: Typing “-20”, “0”, “1e3” and “2.5” into Spots: only digits stay and a lone 0 is ignored; the down arrow stops at 1; a minus in a price is ignored.

cases.title: §20 The Open until line
cases.explanation: The last sentence now names the later date: “You pay each piece within 7 days of it arriving or by that tester's deadline, whichever is later, or the tester can charge you.”

cases.title: §21 Two ticks above Post
cases.explanation: On an older Terms version: “I agree to the updated Terms of Use. Read what changed” first, then the Charge tick, then Post the test.

cases.title: §21 Required
cases.explanation: Unticked, Post is refused: the red line “Tick to agree to the updated Terms of Use.” right under the tick.

cases.title: §21 The updated-Terms tick on Post
cases.explanation: Refused while unticked; ticked, Post goes through (and the account is on the current Terms from then on).

cases.title: §21 On the join page
cases.explanation: Ana, on the older version, gets the same tick above Join this test (no “I'm 18 or older”: age is asked only at sign-up).

cases.title: §21 On the current version
cases.explanation: No tick: just Join this test.

cases.title: §22 A ticked part needs a price
cases.explanation: Recorded session ticked and its price left empty: red on leaving it, “Enter a price for the recording, or tick Free.”

cases.title: §22 Post refused
cases.explanation: Post the test is refused while the ticked part has no price; the list above the button names it and goes to the field.

cases.title: §22 Free
cases.explanation: $0 only through the Free tick: ticking Free clears the red line.

cases.title: §22 A ticked part with no price
cases.explanation: Ticking Recorded session and leaving its price empty turns it red; Post is refused; the Free tick is the way to $0.

cases.title: §22 Save looks disabled
cases.explanation: Nothing changed yet: Save is greyed (its tooltip: “Nothing has changed yet”).

cases.title: §22 “Not saved yet”
cases.explanation: Typed on Edit, then the page reloaded: the changes are back with the badge “Not saved yet” next to Save.

cases.title: §22 “Not posted yet”
cases.explanation: The same on Post: “Not posted yet”.

cases.title: §23 Worked with you on 4 tests
cases.explanation: In the invite panel's People you've worked with, Ana's fold now says how each one went: “Night Market demo · ended”, “Kelp Forest: iPhone beta · left”, “Sky Lab: tutorial · left”, “Harbor Run: lighthouse · in it now”.

cases.title: §24 A working tester's rating stops a press once
cases.explanation: Ana was still working when they rated, which ends their part: Nora's Pay on Ben's answers, pressed on a page opened before it, stops once with “Your Pay on Ben Okafor's written answers didn't go through. Since you opened this page: Ana Silva finished their part (rated you) · 5:17 AM”

cases.title: §24 A working tester rates
cases.explanation: Ana rates Nora just before Nora presses Pay on Ben's answers: the press stops once for “Ana Silva finished their part (rated you)” (Testers leaving), and the second press pays.

cases.title: §24 An ended tester's rating, live
cases.explanation: Cam's work had ended early; Cam rated Nora while the page was open: the live box says “Updated · 7:12 AM: Cam Lee rated you. You can rate them until Nov 12, 2026.” (info only, no reload).

cases.title: §24 Needs you
cases.explanation: The same poll adds “Rate Cam Lee · 14 days left”, linking to Cam's Rate box.

cases.title: §24 An ended tester rates, live
cases.explanation: Cam (whose work had ended) rates Nora while the test page is open: the live line and Needs you's “Rate Cam Lee” arrive without a reload, and Nora's next Pay (on Ben's answers) goes straight through.

cases.title: §25 No stop
cases.explanation: Ben switched a moment before Nora pressed Pay on Ana's answers from a page that hadn't refreshed: the Pay went straight through (“paid $10.00 of $10.00”), since a tester's Switch or Keep never stops a developer press.

cases.title: §25 Switch is a quiet line
cases.explanation: In another tab of Nora's left open, the only sign of it: the live box's line “Ben Okafor switched to the new terms” with “See their contract”.

cases.title: §25 A tester's Switch never stops the developer
cases.explanation: Ben switches to the new terms while Nora's page is open and Nora presses Pay at once: the Pay goes straight through (the only sign of the Switch is a quiet live line, shown in another tab).

cases.title: §26 Nothing changed yet
cases.explanation: Right after sending, “Send my updated answers” is greyed (its tooltip: “Nothing has changed since you sent it”).

cases.title: §26 Changed
cases.explanation: With “ The ramp after it too.” added to the second answer, the button lights up.

cases.title: §26 Changed back
cases.explanation: Deleting the added words makes the answers match what was sent again, and the button greys again.

cases.title: §26 Send waits for a change
cases.explanation: Greyed after sending; typing in an answer lights it up; deleting the typing greys it again (the server also refuses an identical resend with “Nothing has changed since you sent it.”).

cases.title: §27 Four characters
cases.explanation: End early's “Why?” with “Done” (4 characters): red “Say a little more: at least 5 characters.” on leaving the box, and End their work now stays disabled.

cases.title: §27 Five characters
cases.explanation: “Done!” (5 characters): the red line goes and the button is enabled.

cases.title: §27 The same for Stop the test
cases.explanation: Stop's “Are you sure…?” pop-up, its required “Why? (testers read it)” with “Done”: red “Say a little more: at least 5 characters.”

cases.title: §27 At least 5 characters
cases.explanation: End early with “Done” is red and disabled; one more character enables it; Stop the test's reason follows the same rule.

cases.title: §28 The required star
cases.explanation: Written answers aren't listed on this test, so the form asks the one default question “Your feedback”, with its required “*” on the same line as the label (at the right end of that line), not wrapped onto a line of its own.

cases.explanation: /api/health with the key answers {"ok":true,"emails":"degraded: emails"} (HTTP 200: the site itself is up), so a keyword monitor alerts the owner through its own emails and texts.

cases.explanation: The plain /api/health answers only {"ok":true}: the email state is for the keyed monitor.

cases.explanation: The same red box when Resend answered with its daily limit: “Emails aren't sending: 3 waiting since 4:39 AM CDT. Resend's daily limit was reached (free plan: 100 a day). Emails will go out tomorrow, or upgrade the plan.” (set up in the database for the recording).

cases.explanation: Nora's test page (left) and Ana's session page (right) are open the day after Ana's deadline: the 5-minute sweep opens Charge and Ana's page shows Charge and Let it go.

cases.title: (a) The developer's row once Charge is open
cases.explanation: Pay is still there and the “If you don't pay by …” line is gone (the row itself doesn't say Ana can now charge; Nora's bell does).

cases.title: (a) The tester's bell
cases.explanation: “Nora Lane didn't review your written answers in 7 days: charge $10.00 or let it go”.

cases.title: (a) The developer's bell
cases.explanation: ““Harbor Run: first 3 levels”: Ana Silva's written answers waited over 7 days: pay it (Ana Silva can now charge or let it go).”

cases.title: (b) The late joiner still waits: the developer
cases.explanation: The first testers' deadlines have passed, but Cam joined on day 20: Cam's row (sent Oct 18) reads “If you don't pay by Nov 16, Cam Lee can charge you $10.00, their contract price, or let it go.”, Nov 16 being Cam's own deadline.

cases.title: (b) The early tester: Charge is open
cases.explanation: Ben joined on day 1 and sent on day 2 (“sent Tue, Sep 29”); their deadline passed yesterday, so Charge opened and the “If you don't pay by” line is gone.

cases.title: (b) The late joiner's dashboard
cases.explanation: Cam's answers stay under “Waiting for the developer” (“Written answers sent: waiting for review”): no Charge or cancel yet.

cases.title: (b) The early tester's dashboard
cases.explanation: “Charge or cancel 1”: “Parts the developer hasn't reviewed once 7 days have passed since you sent them and your deadline has passed: charge for them, or let them go.” and “Harbor Run: lighthouse · 1 part” with “Charge or let it go →”.

cases.title: (b) After the late joiner's own deadline
cases.explanation: Charge opens for Cam only now: “Nora Lane didn't review your written answers in 7 days: charge $10.00 or let it go.”

cases.title: (b) The late joiner's bell
cases.explanation: “Nora Lane didn't review your written answers in 7 days: charge $10.00 or let it go” arrives only after Cam's own deadline.

cases.title: Rate after the team's Stop: the first press stops
cases.explanation: Ana's Rate and finish, from a page opened before the team stopped the test: “Your Rate didn't go through. Since you opened this page: This test was stopped at <time>.” and “Press Rate again to go ahead.” (the stop time shows twice: “<time>. · <time>”).

cases.title: The second press rates
cases.explanation: The page then reads “You rated Nora Lane.”; its banner says “Nora Lane stopped the test on Oct 29, 2026. You can still ask to show an excerpt and chat. Work you sent is still reviewed.”, although the team stopped it.

cases.title: Rate stops once for the team's Stop
cases.explanation: The team stops the test while Ana's page is open: the first Rate press stops with “This test was stopped at <time>.”, the second rates and the page reads “You rated Nora Lane.”

cases.title: A page opened after the stop
cases.explanation: Ben opens their session page after the team's Stop and rates: the first press goes through (no stop box) and the page reads “You rated Nora Lane.”

cases.title: Opened after the stop
cases.explanation: Ben's page was opened after the team stopped the test, so Rate goes through on the first press.

cases.title: (c) Sent on the last day: the developer
cases.explanation: Dee's deadline passed yesterday, but they sent on their last day (“sent Wed, Oct 28”), so the row reads “If you don't pay by Nov 4, Dee Park can charge you $10.00, their contract price, or let it go.”: 7 days after sending.

cases.title: (c) Sent on the last day: the tester
cases.explanation: “Written answers: Under review”, sent Oct 28: no Charge yet, although Dee's deadline has passed.

cases.title: (c) 7 days after sending: Charge opens
cases.explanation: “Nora Lane didn't review your written answers in 7 days: charge $10.00 or let it go.”, with Charge and Let it go.

cases.title: (c) The tester's bell
cases.explanation: “Nora Lane didn't review your written answers in 7 days: charge $10.00 or let it go”, 7 days after “Work sent: your written answers for “Harbor Run: reef””.

cases.title: (c) Charge closes on D+21
cases.explanation: 15 days after sending, the tester's Charge box says “Charge closes on Nov 4, 2026.”: sent on day D (Oct 14), Charge opened D+7 (Oct 21), the test's close-out was D+14 (Oct 28), this piece closes D+21 (Nov 4), so this piece stays open a week past the close-out.

cases.title: (c) Pay closes on D+21
cases.explanation: The developer's Needs you row for the same piece: “Pay closes on Nov 4, 2026.” (sent on day D (Oct 14), Charge opened D+7 (Oct 21), the test's close-out was D+14 (Oct 28), this piece closes D+21 (Nov 4)).

sections.title: Emails
sections.explanation: Every kind of email the app sends, as received (rendered from the dev outbox's HTML): developer and tester emails, money lines, the bank confirmation, reminders, and the admins' emails.

cases.title: Confirm your email
cases.explanation: Sent at sign-up (HTML part): “Welcome to Playtest! Confirm your email.” with the link, and “The link works for 48 hours.”

cases.title: Reset your password
cases.explanation: After “Forgot your password?”: “Someone (hopefully you) asked to reset the password for <email>.”, “Choose a new password (the link works once, for 60 minutes).” and “If it wasn't you, ignore this email: your password stays the same.”

cases.title: Choose a password
cases.explanation: The same request from an account with no password yet (a Google sign-up): “Your account has no password yet. Choose one here: Choose a password” and “The link works once, for 60 minutes. You can keep using Continue with Google too.”

cases.title: The developer's daily summary
cases.explanation: “Your Playtest summary: 15 updates”: every update since the last email, each with its link: the subscription receipt, joins, sent answers, “Receipt: you paid $10.00 for Ana Silva's written answers”, the booked call and its cancelling, “… is paused and closes on Nov 5 unless you pay what you owe”, “We charged your card $10.00 for what you owed.”, “Your tests are running again” and “Your tests are paused after a chargeback”.

cases.title: The tester's daily summary
cases.explanation: “Your Playtest summary: 8 updates”: “Work sent: your written answers …”, “Nora Lane paid you $10.00 for your written answers …”, “Rate Nora Lane …”, “Your call on Sat, Oct 31 at 3:02 PM UTC was cancelled because the test is paused.”, “… is running again” and “Payment for your work on “Tide Tracker: widgets” may be delayed” (the tester never reads hold or chargeback).

cases.title: Email Off: the bank confirmation
cases.explanation: With email Off only the must-send lines go, in one end-of-day email, “Your Playtest account updates: 1”: “Your bank wants you to confirm a $7.00 payment. Confirm this payment by <date>.” with its link to the piece.

cases.title: Weekly: the payment email
cases.explanation: On Weekly email (their summary not due yet), payment lines go out the same day: “Your Playtest payment updates: 3” with the subscription receipt and “Receipt: you paid $8.00 for Ben Okafor's written answers”.

cases.title: Contact us (to the team)
cases.explanation: “Contact us: A payment” to the team's addresses (named here, not shown): “From Ana Silva <email> · About: A payment” and the message.

cases.title: New chargeback (to every admin)
cases.explanation: “Playtest: new chargeback of $10.00”: “A developer's bank reversed a $10.00 payment (pi_…). The developer's account is on a chargeback hold.” with the link to the console's chargebacks.

cases.title: The admins' daily email
cases.explanation: “Playtest admin: 32 items for the team” (from an earlier media run on Oct 28): one line per item waiting, “New dispute: <tester> vs <developer> on “…”: “<reason>”” and “Hold lift waiting for your Approve: …”, each with its link.
